text.p: Chelsea added to Sunderland's relegation worries in the English premier league with a thumping 6-2 victory at Stamford Bridge on Sunday which featured two goals from Welsh striker Mark Hughes.
Italians Gianfranco Zola and Roberto di Matteo also hit the target as Chelsea, 2-0 ahead at half-time, lifted themselves to seventh in the table to keep alive their hopes of UEFA Cup qualification.

The home side had a brief moment of alarm in the second-half when Sunderland pulled back to 3-2 with goals from Paul Stewart and Alex Rae, but a splendid individual effort from Hughes proved to be the first of three Chelsea goals in the last 12 minutes.

Substitute Gianluca Vialli, despite a suspicion of offside, provided Hughes with an easier chance to make it five and Di Matteo completed the scoring in the last minute to complete a miserable afternoon for French goalkeeper Lionel Perez.
It was Sunderland's sixth defeat in their last seven matches and they remain only three points clear of the relegation zone with seven games remaining.
"We've got to get back to basics and make people work to score goals against us again," said manager Peter Reid.
